title: National System of Microscopy: Advances in the Organization of Microscopy Equipment Accessibility in Argentina
content: Argentina has a long tradition in microscopy applied to biological science. Professor Eduardo Patricio de Robertis (Figure 1) was a great cell biologist and neuroscientist that described among other structures the subcellular organization of the synapses together with Dr Bennet more than 70 years ago. It was a key discovery for neurobiology [1]. In addition, he is considered one of the fathers of the modern Cell Biology spreading the use of microscopy techniques along of Latin American research community. Following theses relevant features and tradition, in the last few years in Argentina was created the National System of Microscopy (SNM) [2] to organize the access of the microscopes available in the country to the users of the different field of research that need them for answer their questions. El SNM has until July 2021 [3] the adhesion of 97 centers of microscopy distributed in the entire country that contain 189 advanced microscopies. However, 57 % of the equipment is still quite ancient (more than 10-years-old) despite the effort to renew it. The fortresses of SNM are based on the high number of centers that have joined it. In addition, besides the increment in the use of this kind of technology, SNM allowed the increment in the number of human resources that have acquired a high level of training. Although this project have good results since started, the continuous economic crisis in Argentina does not allow to renew the equipment. In addition, many PhD and postdoctoral students and in the last year researchers with high level of knowledge in microscopy must move to other countries looking for new opportunities forced for the broken economy. Unfortunately, the funding for scientific programs in Argentina have decreased around 40 % in the last 2 years. Therefore, Argentina should build a long-term strategy to make the SNM more efficient and sustainable over the time.
